extracted.intended_audience: registrants with mining operations, qualified persons (e.g., professional geologists/mining engineers), securities counsel, and compliance officers preparing SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and substantive technical standards for disclosure of exploration results, mineral resources, and mineral reserves in SEC registration statements and reports, including qualified-person responsibilities, study standards (initial assessment, pre-feasibility, feasibility), summary and individual property disclosure, and related filing/consent rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified person signature and dating
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (b)(1)(ii) of this section, if more than one qualified person has prepared the technical report summary, each qualified person must date and sign the technical report summary. The qualified person's signature must comply with § 230.402(e) or § 240.12b-11(d) of this chapter. The technical report summary must also clearly delineate the section or sections of the summary prepared by each qualified person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a third-party firm signs instead (see paragraph (b)(1)(ii)), it may sign without naming the individual employee; otherwise each qualified person signs and dates and identifies which sections they prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party firm may sign technical report summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party firm comprising mining experts, such as professional geologists or mining engineers, may date and sign the technical report summary instead of, and without naming, its employee, member or other affiliated person who prepared the technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a firm signs in lieu of naming individuals, see special consent and reliance rules elsewhere in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of filing technical report summary for reserves/resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must file the technical report summary as an exhibit to the relevant registration statement or other Commission filing when disclosing for the first time mineral reserves or mineral resources or when there is a material change in the mineral reserves or mineral resources from the last technical report summary filed for the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing obligation attaches at first disclosure and upon material change since last filed summary for the property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical report summary filing for exploration results changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant files a technical report summary to support the disclosure of exploration results, it must also file a technical report summary when there is a material change in the exploration results from the last technical report summary filed for the property. In each instance, the registrant must file the technical report summary as an exhibit to the relevant Commission filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material changes to exploration results trigger a new exhibit filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty/streamingholders referencing produced registrant's technical report
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has a royalty, streaming, or other similar right is not required to submit a separate technical report summary for a property that is covered by a current technical report summary filed by the producing mining registrant. In that situation, the registrant holding the royalty, streaming, or other similar right should refer to the producing registrant's previously filed technical report summary in its filing with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reference will not be deemed to incorporate by reference the previously filed technical report summary into the royalty registrant's filing absent an express statement to incorporate by reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception when royalty registrant lacks access to technical report
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has a royalty, streaming, or other similar right is not required to file a technical report summary for an underlying property if the registrant lacks access to the technical report summary because obtaining the information would result in an unreasonable burden or expense; or it requested the technical report summary from the owner/operator who denied the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitting information due to lack of access, the royalty registrant should explain the lack of access and provide required information it does possess without unreasonable burden or expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent of qualified person for use of name/quotations/filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must obtain the written consent of the qualified person to the use of the qualified person's name, or any quotation from, or summarization of, the technical report summary in the relevant registration statement or report, and to the filing of the technical report summary as an exhibit to the registration statement or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple qualified persons prepared sections, obtain written consent from each qualified person pertaining to the sections they prepared; special rules apply when a third-party firm signed the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing/retention of qualified person written consents
rubrics_metrics.description: For Securities Act filings, the registrant must file the written consent as an exhibit to the registration statement pursuant to §§ 230.436 and 230.601(b)(23) of this chapter. For Exchange Act reports, the registrant is not required to file the written consent obtained from the qualified person, but should retain the written consent for as long as it is relying on the qualified person's information and supporting documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Securities Act = file consent exhibit; Exchange Act = retain consent in records while relying on info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of qualified person's employment and affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must state in the filed registration statement or report whether each qualified person who prepared the technical report summary is an employee of the registrant. If the qualified person is not an employee, the registrant must name the qualified person's employer, disclose whether the qualified person or employer is affiliated with the registrant or another entity that has an ownership, royalty, or other interest in the property, and if affiliated, describe the nature of the affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses 'affiliate' as defined in § 230.405 or § 240.12b-2; full transparency on affiliations is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on third‑party specialists allowed but cannot disclaim responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified person may include in the technical report summary information and documentation provided by a third-party specialist who is not a qualified person (e.g., attorney, appraiser, economic or environmental consultant) upon which the qualified person has relied in preparing the technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The qualified person may not disclaim responsibility for any information or documentation prepared by the third-party specialist or any part of the technical report summary based upon that information. Registrant is not required to file the third-party specialist's written consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration target disclosure permitted with special labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may disclose an exploration target for one or more properties that is based upon and accurately reflects information and supporting documentation of a qualified person. The qualified person may include a discussion of an exploration target in a technical report summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any disclosure of an exploration target must appear in a separate section clearly captioned as a discussion of an exploration target, with required prominent statements and supporting explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required prominent statements for exploration targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The exploration-target section must include a clear and prominent statement that: (i) the ranges of potential tonnage and grade are conceptual in nature; (ii) there has been insufficient exploration to estimate a mineral resource; (iii) it is uncertain if further exploration will result in estimating a mineral resource; and (iv) the exploration target does not represent an estimate of a mineral resource or mineral reserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four explicit warnings must be prominent and clear in the exploration-target section to avoid misleading investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration target required supporting information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any disclosure of an exploration target must include: (i) a detailed explanation of the basis (e.g., conceptual geological model); (ii) explanation of the process used to determine ranges of tonnage and grade expressed as approximations; (iii) statement clarifying whether based on actual exploration results or proposed programs including description of exploration activity level, proposed testing, and time frame; and (iv) a statement that ranges could change as proposed activities are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must provide both the basis and the process for the ranges and be explicit about the exploratory status and timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of mineral resources must be based on qualified person's initial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant's disclosure of mineral resources must be based upon a qualified person's initial assessment, which includes and supports the qualified person's determination of mineral resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial assessment must enable determination and support of mineral resource estimates per § 229.1300 definitions and requirements; for material properties, the technical report summary must describe procedures, findings and conclusions as required by § 229.601(b)(96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified person requirements when determining existence of a mineral resource
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining the existence of a mineral resource, a qualified person must: (A) be able to estimate or interpret location, quantity, grade/quality continuity, and other geological characteristics from specific geological evidence and knowledge including sampling; and (B) conclude there are reasonable prospects for economic extraction based on the initial assessment, which must include a qualitative evaluation of relevant technical and economic factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial assessment must establish economic potential and include the qualified person's qualitative evaluation of factors likely to influence extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of mineral resources (measured, indicated, inferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining mineral resources, a qualified person must subdivide mineral resources, in order of increasing geological confidence, into inferred, indicated, and measured mineral resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inferred resources, the qualified person must have reasonable expectation majority could be upgraded with continued exploration and be able to defend that expectation to peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut-off grade estimation and commodity price disclosure in initial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified person must include cut-off grade estimation, based on assumed unit costs for surface or underground operations and estimated mineral prices, in the initial assessment. To estimate mineral prices, the qualified person must use a price for each commodity that provides a reasonable basis for establishing prospects of economic extraction. The qualified person must disclose the price used and explain with particularity reasons and material assumptions, including time frame used to estimate commodity price and unit costs. The selected price and assumptions must be current as of the end of the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual prices may be used if reasonable and disclosed as contractual; full transparency on price selection and time frame is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative assessment of technical and economic factors in initial assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualified person must provide a qualitative assessment of all relevant technical and economic factors likely to influence the prospect of economic extraction to establish economic potential and justify that issues can be resolved with further exploration and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include (but are not limited to) site infrastructure, mine design and planning, processing plant, environmental compliance and permitting, and any other reasonably assumed technical/economic factors (plans, negotiations, agreements with local groups). See Table 1 for assumptions permitted in initial assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow analysis optional in initial assessment; accuracy and contingency if included
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualified person may include cash flow analysis in an initial assessment. If included, operating and capital cost estimates must have an accuracy level of at least approximately ±50% and a contingency level of no greater than 25%. The qualified person must state the accuracy and contingency levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If economic analysis includes inferred resources, additional disclosure rules apply (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure rules when inferred resources used in economic analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: If providing an economic analysis in the initial assessment that includes inferred mineral resources, the qualified person must: (A) state with equal prominence that the assessment is preliminary, includes inferred resources that are too speculative to have modifying factors applied to make them reserves, and there is no certainty the economic assessment will be realized; (B) disclose the percentage of mineral resources used in the cash flow analysis that were classified as inferred; and (C) disclose, with equal prominence, results of the economic analysis excluding inferred resources in addition to results that include them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equal prominence means these cautions and alternative results must appear with the same visibility as other results to prevent misleading presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table 1 factors and expectations by study level
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 1 summarizes relevant factors evaluated in technical studies and describes expectations for site infrastructure, mine design & planning, processing plant, environmental compliance & permitting, and other relevant factors across initial assessment, preliminary feasibility study, and feasibility study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Table 1 as guidance for the appropriate level of detail and testing required at each study stage (e.g., assume infrastructure vs. finalized plans; assumed processing methods vs. pilot plant tests). The number/type of applicable factors depends on the particular mineral/property/project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mineral reserves disclosure must be based on pre-feasibility or feasibility study
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant's disclosure of mineral reserves must be based upon a qualified person's preliminary feasibility (pre-feasibility) study or feasibility study, each of which includes and supports the qualified person's determination of mineral reserves. The study must include detailed evaluation of all applicable modifying factors to demonstrate economic viability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For material properties, the supporting technical report summary must describe procedures, findings and conclusions as required by § 229.601(b)(96).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdivision of mineral reserves into probable and proven
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining mineral reserves, a qualified person must subdivide mineral reserves, in order of increasing confidence, into probable mineral reserves and proven mineral reserves. The determination must be based on application of modifying factors to indicated or measured mineral resources resulting in a determination that part of the resource is economically mineable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and confidence differences explained: probable has lower confidence than proven but sufficient to show economic viability; measured->probable conversion allowed when application of modifying factors lowers confidence; high confidence required for proven.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-feasibility/feasibility study must demonstrate economic viability and life-of-mine plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The pre-feasibility or feasibility study supporting determination of mineral reserves must demonstrate that, at the time of reporting, extraction of the mineral reserve is economically viable under reasonable investment and market assumptions, and must establish a life of mine plan that is technically achievable and economically viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study need not show facilities are in place or permits obtained, but qualified person must have, after reasonable investigation, not identified obstacles to obtaining permits and reasonably believe approvals and sales contracts are highly likely in a timely manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market study requirement in certain reserve circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain circumstances, determination of mineral reserves may require completion of at least a preliminary market study (for pre-feasibility) or a final market study (for feasibility) to support conclusions about chances of obtaining revenues, e.g., where product cannot be traded on an exchange, no established market exists, and no sales contract exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified person must consider adverse impacts from any unresolved material matter contingent on a third party when assessing reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commodity price selection for pre-feasibility/feasibility studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For both pre-feasibility and feasibility studies, a qualified person must use a price for each commodity that provides a reasonable basis for establishing that the project is economically viable. The qualified person must disclose the price used and explain with particularity the reasons and material assumptions, including time frame used to estimate the price and costs; selected price and assumptions must be current as of the end of registrant's most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractual prices may be used if reasonable and disclosed as contractual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic analysis requirements for pre-feasibility and feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-feasibility study must include an economic analysis supporting economic viability assessed by detailed discounted cash flow analysis or similar. A feasibility study must include an economic analysis that describes taxes in detail, estimates revenues, and assesses economic viability by detailed discounted cash flow analysis. Qualified person must use commodity prices meeting paragraph (e)(4) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue estimates may require preliminary or final market study in specific situations (see market study criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of inferred resources from pre-feasibility demonstration of viability
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualified person must exclude inferred mineral resources from the pre-feasibility study's demonstration of economic viability in support of a disclosure of a mineral reserve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inferred resources are too speculative to support reserve economic demonstrations at pre-feasibility stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-feasibility study uncertainty identification and cost accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-feasibility study must identify sources of uncertainty that require further refinement in a final feasibility study. Operating and capital cost estimates in a pre-feasibility study must, at a minimum, have an accuracy level of approximately ±25% and a contingency range not exceeding 15%. The qualified person must state the accuracy level and contingency range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State accuracy and contingency explicitly; list of factors similar to feasibility but at lower detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility study more detailed with tighter cost accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A feasibility study must contain application and description of all relevant modifying factors in more detailed form and with more certainty than a pre-feasibility study. Operating and capital cost estimates in a feasibility study must, at a minimum, have an accuracy level of approximately ±15% and a contingency range not exceeding 10%. The qualified person must state the accuracy level and contingency range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feasibility stage expects finalized plans, pilot tests (if required), detailed schedules, and final assessments of modifying factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion rules between resource and reserve categories
rubrics_metrics.description: If uncertainties preventing conversion of measured mineral resource to a proven mineral reserve no longer exist, the qualified person may convert measured resource to proven reserve. The qualified person cannot convert an indicated mineral resource to a proven mineral reserve unless new evidence first justifies conversion to a measured mineral resource. The qualified person cannot convert an inferred mineral resource to a mineral reserve without first obtaining new evidence that justifies converting it to an indicated or measured mineral resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict progression required: inferred -> indicated/measured -> probable/proven with new evidence or resolution of uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified person may rely on registrant-provided information (categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: The qualified person may indicate in the technical report summary that the qualified person has relied on information provided by the registrant regarding macroeconomic trends, marketing information and plans within the registrant's control, legal matters outside the qualified person's expertise, environmental matters outside the qualified person's expertise, accommodations the registrant commits or plans to provide to local groups, and governmental factors outside the qualified person's expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on registrant-provided information, the qualified person must include a separately captioned section detailing reliance (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required 'Reliance on Information Provided by the Registrant' section
rubrics_metrics.description: In a separately captioned section entitled 'Reliance on Information Provided by the Registrant,' the qualified person must: (i) identify the categories of information provided by the registrant; (ii) identify particular portions of the technical report summary prepared in reliance on that information and the extent of the reliance; and (iii) disclose why the qualified person considers it reasonable to rely upon the registrant for any of the specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section must clearly map which parts of the report depended on registrant-supplied data and justify that reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant-provided descriptions not part of qualified person's certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Any description in the technical report summary or other part of the registration statement of the procedures, findings, and conclusions reached about matters identified by the qualified person as having been based on information provided by the registrant shall not be considered part of the registration statement prepared or certified by the qualified person within the meaning of Sections 7 and 11 of the Securities Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits the scope of what is considered prepared/certified by the qualified person for Securities Act liability purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary disclosure: applicability and properties covered
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has material mining operations and two or more mining properties must provide the information specified for all properties that the registrant: (i) owns or has/probably will have direct/indirect economic interest; (ii) operates or probably will operate under lease/other legal agreement authorizing it as principal to sell/dispose of mineral; or (iii) has or probably will have an associated royalty or similar right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant has only one material property, only individual property disclosure under § 229.1304 is required; royalty registrant lacking access may omit some info if they specify what's missing and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty-only registrant omission and disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant that has a royalty, streaming or similar right, but lacks access to information specified for summary disclosure about underlying properties, may omit such information provided that the registrant: (i) specifies the information to which it lacks access; (ii) explains that it lacks access because obtaining it would be an unreasonable burden/expense or because it requested and was denied the information by a non-affiliated holder; and (iii) provides all required information it does possess or can acquire without unreasonable burden/expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires explicit explanation of omissions and provision of available information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps and overview required in summary disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose: (1) a map or maps of appropriate scale showing the locations of all properties, legible when printed; and (2) an overview of the registrant's mining properties and operations presented in narrative or tabular format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps should be legible on printed page; overview may aggregate information across properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview must include aggregate annual production for three fiscal years
rubrics_metrics.description: The overview must include aggregate annual production for the properties during each of the three most recently completed fiscal years preceding the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate production figures help investors assess scale and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested items to include in overview of properties (aggregate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overview should include, as relevant, location of properties; type and amount of ownership interests; identity of operator(s); titles, mineral rights, leases or options and acreage; stages of properties (exploration, development, production); key permit conditions; mine types and mineralization styles; and processing plants and other available facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant should include disclosure material to investor understanding and may refer to individual property disclosures rather than duplicate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty/licence registrant production disclosure limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant with only a royalty or similar economic interest should provide only the portion of the production that led to royalty or other incomes for each of the three most recently completed fiscal years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit aggregate production disclosure to amounts that led to income for royalty-only registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary table requirement for mineral resources and reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of all mineral resources and mineral reserves, as determined by the qualified person, at the end of the most recently completed fiscal year must be provided by commodity and geographic area and for each property containing 10% or more of the registrant's combined measured and indicated mineral resources or 10% or more of mineral reserves. Provide each class of resources (inferred, indicated, measured) and reserves (probable, proven) together with totals, using the formats in Table 1 (resources) and Table 2 (reserves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include commodity/geographic breakdowns and property-level disclosures for material properties; be sure to follow table formats or reasonable modifications for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic area and exclusivity rules for summary tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'by geographic area' means by individual country, regions of a country, state, groups of states, mining district, or other political units as material. All disclosure of mineral resources by the registrant must be exclusive of mineral reserves. All disclosure of mineral resources and reserves must be only for the portion attributable to the registrant's interest in the property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimates must be for the registrant's attributable portion and resources should not include reserves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Price and point-of-reference disclosure for summary estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Each mineral resource and reserve estimate must be based on a reasonable and justifiable price selected by a qualified person pursuant to § 229.1302(d) or (e), and each estimate called for in Tables 1 and 2 must be based on a specific point of reference selected by a qualified person. The registrant must disclose the selected point of reference for each table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material assumptions related to price estimates must be current as of the end of the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted modifications to tabular formats and currency of assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant may modify the tabular formats in Tables 1 and 2 for ease of presentation or to add information. All material assumptions and information pertaining to the summary disclosure of mineral resources and reserves, including material assumptions related to price estimates, must be current as of the end of the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications are allowed for presentation practicality but must preserve required information and currency of assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual property disclosure obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose the information specified in § 229.1304 for each property that is material to its business or financial condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section § 229.1304 (not included in full in this chunk) details required information for each material property; summary disclosure cross-references individual-property disclosures to avoid duplication.
